# Volume 4 — CHAPTER 13 A GHOSTLY EVENING

!!! note "Source text"
    Passages cited on the wiki pages link into this page. Only volumes at or before
    this page's cutoff are present.

A week afterward, one night, Nell made up her mind to hurry across the meadows to the dwelling up the stream to pay a casual visit. The night was filled with a slate-colored mist that had slunk inside from the gulf, wrapped the port, packed the ravines and dales, and stuck weightily to the fall pastures. The ocean groaned and trembled through the haze. Nell observed Seven Gulls in a different light, discovering that it was uncanny, enigmatic, and intriguing; nevertheless, it likewise made her feel somewhat solitary. Hugh had gone and would not return before the next day, since he was present at a doctor's gathering in Port Marlow. Nell craved sixty minutes of companionship with a female companion. Captain Saul and Miss Winifred were both “good fellows” in their distinct manners; yet youth pined for youth.
{: #nw-v04-c13-p0000 }

“If Isolde or Cressy or Nonie or Mabel were able to drop in for a visit,” she remarked to herself, “it would be so wonderful! A GHOSTLY night like this is rare. Were that masking fog to be abruptly pulled away tonight, I am certain every vessel that ever departed Seven Gulls for its destruction would appear traveling up the harbor, carrying their drowned crews upon their decks. It strikes me as hiding countless secrets—as though I were encircled by the ghosts of former generations of Seven Gulls inhabitants staring at me from behind that gray screen. Should the beloved deceased women of this small home return to see it again, an evening precisely like this one is when they would arrive. Staying seated here much longer will cause me to spot one of them across from me in Hugh’s chair. Tonight, this location feels a bit uncanny. Even Gog and Magog seem to be perking up their ears so as to detect the strides of invisible visitors. Before my own imagination terrifies me, just as it did in the past regarding the Whispering Wood, I will rush over to visit Lorna. I shall leave my house of dreams behind so it can greet its former residents. They will receive my goodwill and welcome from my fire—prior to my return they will have departed, and my home shall belong to me again. I feel certain it is meeting with history tonight.”
{: #nw-v04-c13-p0001 }

Although she smiled slightly at her own imagination, Nell felt a chilling feeling along her backbone as she blew a kiss to Gog and Magog, stepping into the mist while carrying a few recent magazines beneath her arm to give to Lorna.
{: #nw-v04-c13-p0002 }

“Lorna is crazy about books and magazines,” Miss Winifred had mentioned to her, “and she scarcely ever gets a look at one. Buying them or paying for subscriptions is beyond her means. Her poverty is truly pitiful, Nell. How she manages to subsist at all on the meager rent that the farm yields is a mystery to me. She does not ever drop a single hint complaining about her lack of money, but I am well aware of what she endures. It has been a burden to her for her entire life. In the days when she was unencumbered and full of ambition, it did not bother her, but it must be painful now, believe ME. It makes me happy that she appeared so cheerful and lively on the night she was over at your place. Captain Saul informed me that he was forced to actually place her coat and cap on her and shove her out the doorway. Do not delay too much before visiting her, either. Should you take too long, she will assume it stems from your dislike of looking at Rufus, causing her to retreat right back into her shell. Rufus is a huge, gentle baby, yet that absurd grin and laugh of his do agitate the nerves of certain folks. Fortunately for me, I am not troubled by nerves. My liking for Rufus Vane is greater now than it ever was during the time he possessed his proper faculties—although the Lord is aware that is not saying much. One day during housecleaning season I was down at her place giving Lorna a little help, and I happened to be frying doughnuts. Rufus was hovering about hoping to catch one, as he always does, when suddenly he grabbed a boiling hot one that I had only just scooped out and flipped it onto the nape of my neck as I was stooping down. After that, he chuckled and chuckled. Believe ME, Nell, I needed every bit of God’s grace in my heart to refrain from simply grabbing that pot of sizzling fat and dumping it right over his head.”
{: #nw-v04-c13-p0003 }

Nell chuckled about the anger of Miss Winifred while she hurried through the blackness. Laughter, however, fit poorly with such a night. By the time she arrived at the residence amidst the willows, she was quite solemn. All was extremely quiet. Because the forward section of the dwelling appeared unlit and abandoned, Nell stole around to the side entrance, which led from the veranda into a small sitting room. At that spot, she paused without making a sound.
{: #nw-v04-c13-p0004 }

The door had been left unclosed. Past it, Lorna Vane was sitting inside the faintly illuminated space, her head resting on her arms which were stretched across the table. She was crying terribly—her low, intense, gasping sobs sounding as though an inner torment was attempting to rip its way free from her soul. Next to her sat an aged black dog, who had placed his nose upon her lap, his large canine eyes completely filled with silent, pleading compassion and loyalty. Nell stepped backward in alarm. It seemed to her that she must not intrude upon such sorrow. Her own heart pained with a compassion she could not express. Entering at this moment would mean permanently closing the door on any potential aid or companionship. A certain intuition alerted Nell that the haughty, resentful girl would fail to ever pardon anyone who caught her unawares in such a helpless state of hopelessness.
{: #nw-v04-c13-p0005 }

Stealthily leaving the veranda, Nell made her path through the yard. On the other side, voices echoed in the darkness, accompanied by the faint radiance of a light. Reaching the gate, she encountered two men—Captain Saul carrying a lantern, and a companion who she realized could only be Rufus Vane—a large individual, severely overweight, possessing a wide, circular, florid face, and expressionless eyes. Despite the dim illumination, Nell formed the feeling that his eyes possessed an extraordinary quality.
{: #nw-v04-c13-p0006 }

“Mistress Carrow, is that you?” Captain Saul inquired. “Come, come, walking around by yourself on such a night isn't right. Getting lost in this fog is all too easy. Wait right here until Rufus is safely through the door, and then I will return to guide you across the fields with my light. Dr. Carrow must not return to discover you tumbled right off Cape Leforce because of the fog. It happened to a woman once, four decades back.
{: #nw-v04-c13-p0007 }

“So you went across to visit Lorna,” he remarked, once he returned to her side.
{: #nw-v04-c13-p0008 }

“I remained outside,” Nell stated, before describing the things she had witnessed. A sigh escaped Captain Saul.
{: #nw-v04-c13-p0009 }

“Unfortunate, unfortunate, young girl! She rarely weeps, Mistress Carrow—she possesses too much courage for that. She has to be hurting terribly whenever she actually weeps. Such a night is difficult for miserable females who carry griefs. It has a quality that somewhat resurrects everything we have endured—or dreaded.”
{: #nw-v04-c13-p0010 }

“It is completely haunted,” Nell remarked, shuddering. “I crossed over for that very reason—my wish was to hold a living person’s hand and listen to a living person’s voice.”
{: #nw-v04-c13-p0011 }

“A multitude of INHUMAN presences appear to be lurking around this evening. My very own beloved home was packed with them as well. In fact, they pushed me right out. Thus, I escaped to this spot seeking company among my own species.”
{: #nw-v04-c13-p0012 }

“However, Mistress Carrow, it was correct of you to refrain from entering. Lorna would have disapproved. She would have objected to me entering alongside Rufus, which I would have carried out had I not encountered you. I retained Rufus by my side throughout the entire day. I maintain him in my company as frequently as possible in order to assist Lorna somewhat.”
{: #nw-v04-c13-p0013 }

“Does he not have a strange look in his eyes?” Nell inquired.
{: #nw-v04-c13-p0014 }

“Did you observe that? Indeed, one eye is blue while the other is hazel—a trait inherited from his father. The Vane family possesses that distinct characteristic. It was precisely how I identified him as Rufus Vane upon initially spotting him down in Cuby. Had it not been for the appearance of his eyes, his beard and weight might have prevented me from recognizing him. I suppose you are aware that I was the one who discovered him and escorted him back home. Miss Winifred continually maintains that I ought not to have done so, yet I am unable to concur with her view. Doing so was the RIGHT action—making it the sole option available. I possess no doubts whatsoever regarding THAT. Nevertheless, my aging heart grieves for Lorna. At merely twenty-eight years old, she has endured far greater grief than the majority of women experience over the course of eighty years.”
{: #nw-v04-c13-p0015 }

For a short time, their walk continued without a word. Before long, Nell remarked, “Are you aware, Captain Saul, that carrying a lantern during a walk is something I never enjoy? The oddest sensation always comes over me that a loop of sneaky, malevolent beings encompasses me just beyond the light's reach, right past its dark perimeter, observing me with inimical eyes from the gloom. Since I was a child, I have experienced that emotion. Why should that be? Such a feeling never comes over me when the dark actually encompasses me—when I am totally surrounded by it—I do not feel at all afraid.”
{: #nw-v04-c13-p0016 }

“I share a similar sentiment,” Captain Saul conceded. “My belief is that the dark acts as a companion when it surrounds us tightly. However, when we kind of shove it back—severing our connection to it, in a manner of speaking, through the glow of a lantern—it turns into an adversary. Still, the mist is dispersing.
{: #nw-v04-c13-p0017 }

“If you pay attention, a clever west wind is picking up. By the time you reach home, the stars will have appeared.”
{: #nw-v04-c13-p0018 }

The pair had gone; and upon Nell’s return to her house of dreams, the hearth still held glowing red embers, while every haunting presence had departed.
{: #nw-v04-c13-p0019 }
